prompt: A chemist models the rate of a reaction at concentration $c$ (moles per liter) by $R(c) = \frac{c^2 - 25}{c - 5}$ grams per second. The formula is undefined at exactly $c = 5$. What value does the rate approach as $c \to 5$?
hint: "Undefined at $c = 5$" is just a hole in the formula. The limit asks what the rate is heading toward, so factor.

hints.text: "Undefined at $c = 5$" is just a hole in the formula. The limit asks what the rate is heading toward, so factor.
That leaves $c + 5$, and as $c \to 5$ it heads to $10$ grams per second.

explanation: As $c \to 5$, the rate approaches $5 + 5 = 10$ grams per second.

alternativeExplanations.title: Nudge the concentration
steps: A chemist would simply report the rate at $c = 5$ as $10$ — the hole is an artifact of the formula, not of the chemistry.
